title: 6.16.3 Sub-build: The arm turns
description: One bar, one pointer, one angle. Aim before there is a wall.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The bar sits flat. Moving the pointer does nothing.

steps.title: Turn it toward the pointer
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, set `arm.rotation = arm.angleTo(mouse.x, mouse.y);`. The bar should point at the pointer like a hand on a clock.
hints: `angleTo` returns degrees, the same unit `.rotation` uses.
A bar is drawn from its centre, so it rotates about the middle.

steps.title: Keep it out of the ground
steps.instructions: Clamp the angle with `constrain(angle, -170, -10)` so the arm cannot point straight down.
hints: Without the clamp the arm points into the ground and the shot goes nowhere useful.

requirements.title: The arm follows the pointer
requirements.description: The rotation comes from angleTo the pointer. Help: 6.16.2 (Reading: An arm that turns to the aim)

requirements.title: It stays out of the ground
requirements.description: The angle is limited with constrain, min/max or an if. Help: 6.16.2 (Reading: An arm that turns to the aim)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: The arm turns". The task: turn the arm toward the pointer every frame with angleTo and keep the angle within limits so it cannot point into the ground. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Limited
rubric.description: A clamp keeps it above the ground.
